title: Sonnet 18 (Shall I compare thee to a summer's day?)
author: William Shakespeare
edition: Shakespeare's Sonnets, sonnet XVIII. The source's curly apostrophes (U+2019) are written here as ASCII "'" so the aligner's normaliser sees one apostrophe character throughout.
source: Project Gutenberg eBook 1041, 'Shakespeare's Sonnets', https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/1041/pg1041.txt (sonnet XVIII, line 327 onward), retrieved 2026-10-11. This is the text source the LibriVox page itself cites. Public domain in the US.
verbatim: Shall I compare thee to a summer's day? Thou art more lovely and more temperate: Rough winds do shake the darling buds of May, And summer's lease hath all too short a date: Sometime too hot the eye of heaven shines, And often is his gold complexion dimm'd, And every fair from fair sometime declines, By chance, or nature's changing course untrimm'd: But thy eternal summer shall not fade, Nor lose possession of that fair thou ow'st, Nor shall death brag thou wander'st in his shade, When in eternal lines to time thou grow'st, So long as men can breathe, or eyes can see, So long lives this, and this gives life to thee.
display:
Shall I compare thee to a summer's day? Thou art more lovely and more temperate: Rough winds do shake the darling buds of May, And summer's lease hath all too short a date:

Sometime too hot the eye of heaven shines, And often is his gold complexion dimm'd, And every fair from fair sometime declines, By chance, or nature's changing course untrimm'd:

But thy eternal summer shall not fade, Nor lose possession of that fair thou ow'st, Nor shall death brag thou wander'st in his shade, When in eternal lines to time thou grow'st,

So long as men can breathe, or eyes can see, So long lives this, and this gives life to thee.
notes: 14 readers (S7). 14 lines / ~115 tokens; the page gives per-file lengths of
1:05 to 1:33 including the LibriVox intro and outro, so roughly 45-60 s of
poem each.
TODO(human) - MFA DICTIONARY (OOV) RISK, worse here than for the other texts.
The archaic elisions "dimm'd", "untrimm'd", "ow'st", "wander'st" and
"grow'st" are almost certainly OOV in the default English dictionary, and so
are 'thee', 'thou', 'thy' and 'hath' in some dictionaries. Five OOV tokens in
115 is a high enough rate to corrupt word indices across the whole sonnet.
Either add pronunciations for them to the MFA dictionary or expect this text
to need an override per reader. Resolve this BEFORE counting s7 as a usable
envelope text - it is the most likely of the three to fail alignment QC.

need their own dataset/texts/overrides/<file_id>.txt, and a reading with an
